note: Selective VEGFR-1/2/3 TKIs in biomarker-unselected HCC: the 2006 KRN951/tivozanib rat panel (SK-HEP-1 liver xenograft) predicted class activity, axitinib's placebo-controlled second-line trial then missed its OS primary (2015) while apatinib's AHELP met it (2021), so the xenograft track ends contradicted; animal blood-pressure findings predicted the hypertension seen in HCC patients.
label: HCC (VEGFR TKIs)

engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (fc.py scrape). The PD readouts (tumour-endothelial pVEGFR2 and CD31 microvessel density in A549, DCE-MRI Ktrans in Calu-6) were measured in the lung-xenograft arms of the same rat panel; the SK-HEP-1 liver arm read tumour volume only.
engagement.model: Human liver-cancer cell-line xenografts in athymic rats and nude mice (KRN951 rat panel incl. SK-HEP-1; apatinib HCC mouse xenografts)
engagement.note: KRN951 (tivozanib) lowered tumour-endothelial pVEGFR2, microvessel density and DCE-MRI permeability in rat xenografts; no HCC patient had been dosed with a member drug.
engagement.short: Rat xenograft pVEGFR2 and MVD fell; no patients yet
engagement.quote: Following p.o. administration to athymic rats, KRN951 decreased the microvessel density within tumor xenografts and attenuated VEGFR-2 phosphorylation levels in tumor endothelium.
engagement.judgement: Opens the strip at the first public member-drug liver xenograft. One xenograft track pools the Kirin rat panel (tivozanib) and the later apatinib HCC mouse xenografts (Yang 2018): same system (immunodeficient rodent, human liver-cancer cell line, tumour-volume and vascular readouts) and same prediction.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Fountzilas 2020 and McNamara 2015. McNamara's abstract says 'Two-week perfusion changes were noted on functional imaging' without direction or magnitude, so the DCE comparison could not be scored from what I read.
engagement.model: Human liver-cancer cell-line xenografts in athymic rats and nude mice (KRN951 rat panel incl. SK-HEP-1; apatinib HCC mouse xenografts)
engagement.note: HCC patients on tivozanib showed a fall in plasma soluble VEGFR2 and axitinib patients showed DCE perfusion changes; neither is the model's tissue readout (tumour pVEGFR2, MVD).
engagement.short: Plasma sVEGFR2 fell; model readout never measured
engagement.quote: A significant decrease in soluble plasma VEGFR-2 was noted, assuring adequate target engagement.
engagement.reason: Human readouts differ from model's tissue PD
engagement.judgement: Kept untested rather than a downstream same, following the HCC sibling tile's rule that a circulating protein is a different quantity from tumour-endothelial pVEGFR2 or MVD. The closest human analogue of the model's DCE-MRI Ktrans readout is McNamara 2015 (axitinib, HCC, NCT01273662), whose abstract reports perfusion changes without direction; a checker with that full text could turn this entry into a downstream same for axitinib (product_in_model false). The tivozanib first-in-human DCE perfusion reduction cited in the 2021 FDA review was in mixed solid tumours, not HCC, and is not scored.

dose.confidence_note: Full text read (fc.py scrape); the simulated rat steady-state serum level at 0.2 mg/kg is in the Results, which I did not extract numerically.
dose.model: Human liver-cancer cell-line xenografts in athymic rats and nude mice (KRN951 rat panel incl. SK-HEP-1; apatinib HCC mouse xenografts)
dose.note: SK-HEP-1 liver xenografts were inhibited at 0.2 and 1 mg/kg/day in rats and a steady-state serum level was simulated; no human exposure target was stated.
dose.short: Rat effective dose; no human target stated
dose.quote: The serum concentration of KRN951 at steady state after repeated p.o. administrations of a 0.2 mg/kg dose was simulated as described previously (19).
dose.judgement: Opening entry. The 2021 FDA tivozanib review repeats the rat panel (0.2 and 1 mg/kg/day, TGI in 11/15 and 14/15 lines including liver) but states no exposure multiple against the clinical dose, so there is no target to compare.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Tivozanib's HCC RP2D (1 mg) sits below the 1.34 mg RCC dose and was set by 3+3 tolerability; no source I read relates HCC-patient exposure to the rat-effective serum level.
dose.model: Human liver-cancer cell-line xenografts in athymic rats and nude mice (KRN951 rat panel incl. SK-HEP-1; apatinib HCC mouse xenografts)
dose.note: HCC doses were set by tolerability or carried over from other tumours (tivozanib 1 mg 3/1; axitinib 5 mg BID; apatinib 750 mg), never against a model exposure target.
dose.short: HCC doses set by tolerability, not model
dose.quote: Using a 3+3 design, the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of tivozanib was determined to be 1 mg per os once daily, 21 days on-7 days off.
dose.reason: No HCC-model exposure target to compare
dose.judgement: Not scored 'reached, failed' for axitinib: the efficacious-plasma-concentration work in the axitinib NDA (NonclinPharm-003) used melanoma, colon and lung xenografts, not a liver model, so this track states no target that the 5 mg BID HCC dose could be said to reach; the axitinib failure is counted once, in efficacy. Apatinib's 750 mg AHELP dose likewise has no HCC-model exposure anchor (Yang 2018 gives mouse doses, no exposure).

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (fc.py scrape): Table 2 lists SK-HEP-1 (Liver) with TGI 59.4% at 0.2 mg/kg and 89.9% at 1 mg/kg, both significant. SK-HEP-1 is of endothelial origin although used as a liver-cancer line. model_filed true: the 2021 FDA tivozanib review lists the 15-line nude-rat panel including liver.
efficacy.model: Human liver-cancer cell-line xenografts in athymic rats and nude mice (KRN951 rat panel incl. SK-HEP-1; apatinib HCC mouse xenografts)
efficacy.note: KRN951 (tivozanib) inhibited SK-HEP-1 liver xenografts in athymic rats by 59% and 90% at 0.2 and 1 mg/kg/day; no HCC trial of a member drug existed.
efficacy.quote: The antitumor effects of KRN951 on various human tumors were evaluated in athymic rat xenograft models of breast, colon, hepatic, lung, ovarian, pancreatic, and prostate tumors.
efficacy.judgement: Earliest public member-drug liver xenograft I found. Tian 2011 (apatinib, Cancer Sci) names no tumour types in its abstract and the PMC record carries no full text; no axitinib HCC xenograft before 2015 was found (PubMed, abstract level).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: model: 59-90% tumour growth inhibition (SK-HEP-1); trial: OS HR 0.907 (95% CI 0.646-1.274), primary endpoint missed, while secondary PFS/TTP favoured axitinib (P<0.01); not commensurable
efficacy.population: Unselected, Child-Pugh A, progressed on or intolerant to one prior antiangiogenic therapy
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Kang 2015; quote verbatim in the abstract. Registry results (NCT01210495) posted 2015-05-27, before the September 2015 online publication, so year is 2015 either way.
efficacy.model: Human liver-cancer cell-line xenografts in athymic rats and nude mice (KRN951 rat panel incl. SK-HEP-1; apatinib HCC mouse xenografts)
efficacy.note: Axitinib plus BSC versus placebo in second-line HCC (n=202) missed its OS primary endpoint (HR 0.907), contradicting the liver-xenograft prediction of class activity.
efficacy.short: Axitinib phase 2 missed OS vs placebo
efficacy.quote: Axitinib/BSC did not improve OS over placebo/BSC in the overall population or in stratification subgroups.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: the trial paper does not cite the rat panel. Contra because the primary endpoint (OS, placebo-controlled) failed; the significant PFS/TTP/CBR gains are the tumour-growth signal the xenograft actually predicts, so the miss is on the outcome the trial chose, not on antitumour activity, which is why confidence is medium. Sibling drug in the model (tivozanib) and axitinib in patients: product_in_model false. McNamara 2015 (single-arm, primary 16-week tumour control met) is recorded but a single-arm response endpoint does not set the status against a randomised miss.

patient_trials.quote: Improvements favouring axitinib/BSC (P < 0.01) were observed in secondary efficacy end point analyses [progression-free survival (PFS), time to tumour progression (TTP), and clinical benefit rate (CBR)], and were retained among Asian patients in the prespecified subgroup analyses.
With 42.3% tumor control at 16 weeks, primary endpoint was met.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: apatinib HCC xenograft growth inhibition and prolonged mouse survival (Yang 2018, figure-level, not extracted) vs AHELP OS HR 0.785; not commensurable
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Qin 2021 and Yang 2018. Yang and Qin 2018 (apatinib in six HCC lines and a mouse xenograft) was published by the AHELP principal investigator's group while the trial was enrolling (2014-2017) and before its 2020 readout, so it is prospective; model_filed false because rivoceranib has no FDA NDA (manifest: 'no NDA/BLA').
efficacy.model: Human liver-cancer cell-line xenografts in athymic rats and nude mice (KRN951 rat panel incl. SK-HEP-1; apatinib HCC mouse xenografts)
efficacy.note: AHELP: apatinib improved OS over placebo in second-line HCC (8.7 vs 6.8 months, HR 0.785), matching the xenografts for one member; the 2015 axitinib miss keeps the track contradicted.
efficacy.short: Apatinib AHELP OS win; axitinib miss still rules
efficacy.quote: Overall survival was significantly improved in the apatinib group compared with the placebo group (median 8·7 months [95% CI 7·5‒9·8] vs 6·8 months [5·7‒9·1]; hazard ratio 0·785 [95% CI 0·617‒0·998], p=0·048).
efficacy.reason: Axitinib OS miss outweighs apatinib OS win
efficacy.judgement: strengthens is set because the lint requires it on a same-status entry; read it as 'status unchanged', not as evidence for the contra, since this entry records a same for apatinib. The track status as of 2021 stays contra under 'one drug's contra still beats another drug's same on the same track': the same system predicted class activity, axitinib missed OS against placebo (2015) and apatinib matched (2021) in a near-identical second-line placebo-controlled design. No tier 1-4 source shows the axitinib signal attenuated, so patient_signal_reversed stays false. CARES-310 (camrelizumab plus rivoceranib vs sorafenib, PFS and OS met) is a combination with an anti-PD-1 antibody and is recorded, not scored. Fountzilas 2020 (tivozanib phase 1b/2, 24-week median PFS, ORR 21%, 'did not proceed to stage 2') is ambiguous as a primary-endpoint result and is recorded only. Lin 2020 (single-arm axitinib, DCR 62%) likewise.

patient_trials.quote: Apatinib significantly improved overall survival in patients with pretreated advanced hepatocellular carcinoma compared with placebo, with a manageable safety profile.

Median overall survival was significantly extended with camrelizumab-rivoceranib versus sorafenib (22·1 months [95% CI 19·1-27·2] vs 15·2 months [13·0-18·5]; HR 0·62 [95% CI 0·49-0·80]; one-sided p<0·0001).
Although this study did not proceed to stage 2, there was an early efficacy signal with a very favourable toxicity profile.
The disease control rate was 62.2%, and the response rate was 6.7%, according to RECIST criteria.

efficacy.population: Unselected (four resected HCC patients of different aetiologies)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (open access, full text not read). The lines were generated by six-month orthotopic growth in immunodeficient mice and then screened in vitro; the four donor patients were not treated with axitinib.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived primary-like HCC cell lines generated by orthotopic transplantation, in vitro drug screen
efficacy.note: Four patient-derived HCC lines ranked from non-responder to responder on axitinib in vitro; no patient received the drug, so nothing was compared.
efficacy.short: Patient-derived lines ranked on axitinib; no patients
efficacy.quote: Moreover, the four etiological different liver cancer cell lines displayed differences in the response to 5-FU, Sorafenib, Axitinib, and interferon-alpha treatment, ranking from non-responders to responders depending on the applicated medication.
efficacy.reason: No patient comparison for the screen
efficacy.judgement: A distinct system from the cell-line xenograft track (patient tumour, no immortalised line, patient-selection intent), so its own track. Untested, not blank: the model exists and was run with a member drug, but the source makes no patient comparison. The HCC organoid biobanks scored on the sibling multikinase tile tested sorafenib or lenvatinib, outside this member list, and are not duplicated here.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic murine HCC allograft in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice (apatinib monotherapy, NK-dependent; Yang 2020)
efficacy.note: Apatinib alone attenuated tumour growth and normalised vessels in a syngeneic immunocompetent HCC mouse; AHELP had not yet reported.
efficacy.short: Syngeneic mouse: apatinib slowed tumours; AHELP unreported
efficacy.quote: Here, using a syngeneic HCC mouse model, we demonstrated that treatment with apatinib resulted in attenuation of tumor growth and increased tumor vessel normalization.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Cancer Gene Therapy, paywalled). The host strain (C57BL/6) is named on the article page; the tumour line is not confirmed from what I read. Manuscript received 2019-12-28, before AHELP's first public readout (ASCO abstract issued 2020-05-20).
efficacy.judgement: Own track: an immunocompetent syngeneic allograft with a murine tumour and intact NK/T cells is a different system from the human cell-line xenografts in immunodeficient rodents the draft pools; the prediction (class activity in HCC) is the same, and the brief makes each system a track. Opens untested at first public use.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic murine HCC allograft in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice (apatinib monotherapy, NK-dependent; Yang 2020)
efficacy.note: AHELP: apatinib improved OS over placebo in second-line HCC (HR 0.785), matching the syngeneic allograft's prediction of monotherapy activity.
efficacy.short: AHELP OS win matched syngeneic-mouse prediction
efficacy.quote: Overall survival was significantly improved in the apatinib group compared with the placebo group (median 8·7 months [95% CI 7·5‒9·8] vs 6·8 months [5·7‒9·1]; hazard ratio 0·785 [95% CI 0·617‒0·998], p=0·048).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Yang 2020 and Qin 2021. Timing: Yang 2020 was received 2019-12-28 and accepted 2020-05-29; AHELP's primary result first appeared as an ASCO abstract issued 2020-05-20 (Crossref), so the model was run before the result was public and retrodiction is false. The paper's own aim was the anti-PD-1 combination; the monotherapy arm is what is scored.
efficacy.reason: Apatinib shrank syngeneic tumours; AHELP OS met
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: the trial paper does not cite the syngeneic model. Same, direction only: apatinib monotherapy attenuated tumour growth in the immunocompetent allograft and AHELP met its OS primary against placebo. Only apatinib has been run in this system, so no other member's miss bears on the track. CARES-310 (camrelizumab plus rivoceranib), the combination this model was built to explain, is recorded, not scored.

patient_trials.quote: Apatinib significantly improved overall survival in patients with pretreated advanced hepatocellular carcinoma compared with placebo, with a manageable safety profile.

Median overall survival was significantly extended with camrelizumab-rivoceranib versus sorafenib (22·1 months [95% CI 19·1-27·2] vs 15·2 months [13·0-18·5]; HR 0·62 [95% CI 0·49-0·80]; one-sided p<0·0001).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: attenuation of tumour growth in syngeneic mice (figure-level, abstract read) vs AHELP OS HR 0.785; not commensurable

efficacy.model: Patient-derived liver-cancer stem-cell clones (MEF-feeder culture) supplying a 12-gene prognostic signature; TCGA-LIHC C1/C2 subtypes with axitinib sensitivity imputed in silico (oncoPredict, GDSC-trained)
efficacy.note: LCSC-derived 12-gene signature splits TCGA-LIHC into C1/C2; oncoPredict imputes C2 patients axitinib-sensitive; no patient was treated by subtype.
efficacy.short: C2 subtype imputed axitinib-sensitive; no patients
efficacy.quote: Patients of the C2 subtype, which is closely related to the extracellular matrix, were found to be sensitive to treatments such as Cisplatin, Axitinib, JAK1 inhibitors, WNT-c59, Sorafenib, and RO-3306.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (Europe PMC, open access). The axitinib call is an oncoPredict ridge-regression imputation on TCGA-LIHC transcriptomes trained on GDSC cell-line IC50s, stratified by a consensus-cluster subtype built on 12 LCSC-high prognostic genes; sixteen LCSC strains were isolated from 24 tissues and ten were tumorigenic in mice, but no clone and no patient was exposed to axitinib.
efficacy.reason: No patient dosed by LCSC subtype
efficacy.judgement: Own track rather than the draft's hcc-patient-derived-primary-cell-lines: different model (stem-cell clones on MEF feeders plus a GDSC-trained imputation, versus mouse-passaged primary lines exposed to the drug in vitro) and different prediction (a transcriptomic subtype class, versus a per-donor responder ranking). model_kind in_silico because the axitinib sensitivity was computed, not measured; the checker's 'patient-derived LCSC line' framing describes the signature's source, not the drug test. Untested, not blank: the model exists, names a member drug, and nobody compared it with treated patients.
efficacy.population: Unselected (TCGA-LIHC transcriptomes stratified by LCSC-gene subtype; C2 = extracellular-matrix-high)

safety.confidence_note: Proxy opening: a member drug was in phase I by 2006, so its GLP toxicology and safety-pharmacology package existed; the axitinib review in the bundle gives no IND review date and the tivozanib review gives none I could find.
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology and cardiovascular safety pharmacology in rodent plus dog or monkey
safety.note: Tivozanib (KRN951) was in phase I in 2006, so the species package was in use; its findings stayed unpublished, so no comparison was possible.
safety.short: Species package in use; tox unpublished
safety.quote: KRN951 is currently in phase I clinical development for the treatment of patients with advanced cancer.
safety.judgement: One safety track pools the standard rodent plus non-rodent package for the class (mouse/rat/dog for axitinib, rat/monkey for tivozanib): same system and same rules, as the HCC sibling tile did. The species differ, which is the main reason a checker might split it.

safety.magnitude_basis: blood-pressure rise in mice (30 mg/kg), rats (>=300 mg/kg) and dogs vs clinical hypertension; the review gives no exposure multiple for the cardiovascular studies
safety.confidence_note: Quote verbatim in the bundled 202324 Pharmacology Review (page 4); the patient side is the renal-cell-carcinoma NDA population.
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology and cardiovascular safety pharmacology in rodent plus dog or monkey
safety.note: FDA reviewer pairs the mouse, rat and dog systolic-pressure rise with the hypertension seen in axitinib trials; imported from the RCC NDA.
safety.short: Animal BP rise matched clinical hypertension
safety.quote: Cardiovascular effects of axitinib may include increased systolic blood pressure and a concomitant decrease in heart rate, as demonstrated in mice, rats and dogs. Hypertension was observed in clinical trials conducted with axitinib.
safety.judgement: Comparison stated by the reviewer. The same review notes bone, teeth, spleen/thymus and lipid findings 'not observed clinically', which it attributes to immature animals and does not pair as a miss; not scored opposite because the review gives the margin and the relevance caveat rather than a prediction for adults.

safety.magnitude_basis: animal systolic-pressure rise vs 54% any-grade hypertension in HCC patients on axitinib 5 mg BID; no exposure multiple stated for the animal cardiovascular studies
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Kang 2015; the placebo-arm hypertension rate is not in the abstract.
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology and cardiovascular safety pharmacology in rodent plus dog or monkey
safety.note: The predicted hypertension appeared in HCC patients: 54% of axitinib-treated patients in the randomised phase 2, alongside diarrhoea (54%).
safety.short: 54% hypertension in HCC matched animal BP
safety.quote: Most common all-causality adverse events with axitinib/BSC were diarrhoea (54%), hypertension (54%), and decreased appetite (47%).
safety.judgement: Paired by me (FDA 2012 animal cardiovascular findings vs Kang 2015 HCC safety) to bring the imported RCC comparison into this disease. Diarrhoea was also predicted (gastrointestinal toxicity in mice and dogs). Hand-foot syndrome is not scored against the animals: no rodent or dog shows it.

safety.magnitude_basis: class animal blood-pressure rise vs grade 3-4 hypertension 28% vs 2% on apatinib in AHELP
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Qin 2021. Apatinib's own toxicology is unpublished (no FDA NDA; CRLs were manufacturing-related), so the model side is the class package via axitinib (product_in_model false). The 2021 FDA tivozanib review adds telemetered-monkey hypertension at 3 mg/kg (43-fold HED), a stated margin far above the human dose.
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology and cardiovascular safety pharmacology in rodent plus dog or monkey
safety.note: AHELP: grade 3-4 hypertension in 28% of apatinib versus 2% of placebo patients, the harm the class's animal cardiovascular studies predicted.
safety.quote: The most common treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or 4 were hypertension (71 [28%] patients in the apatinib group vs three [2%] in the placebo group)
safety.reason: Animal BP rise matched HCC hypertension
safety.judgement: Direction only: the harm was predicted but the animal margin (monkey 43-fold HED for tivozanib; rat >=300 mg/kg for axitinib) misplaces it, since patients are hypertensive at the clinical dose. Thrombocytopenia (13%) and hand-foot syndrome (18%) in AHELP are not scored: the first is not in the quoted animal findings I read, the second cannot be shown by the species.
